title: Lesson 2: Le café
description: A café dialogue for ordering breakfast and practicing articles, preferences, and simple service phrases.

notes.1: vous désirez ? literally means you desire?. In a café or shop, it is a natural way to ask What would you like?
notes.2: un café is both a beverage (a coffee) and the place where you drink it (a café). If you order un café in France, you will get a shot of espresso without milk, also called un expresso or un express.
notes.3: Although s'il vous plaît (if it pleases you) may seem very formal, it isn't. It just means please.
notes.4: une tartine beurrée (or simply une tartine) is a slice of buttered bread, a popular breakfast alternative to a croissant. Beurré is the adjective formed from le beurre, butter. In this sentence, it agrees with the feminine noun une tartine, so another -e is added: beurrée.
notes.5: le déjeuner means lunch, so le petit-déjeuner, literally small lunch, is breakfast.
notes.6: All French nouns have a gender: they are either masculine or feminine. A masculine noun is indicated by un/le, a/the, and a feminine noun by une/la. French does not have a separate word for one, so un café can mean a coffee or one coffee, depending on the context.

lines.english: Sir, Madam, what would you like (you desire)?

lines.french: Deux cafés et deux croissants, s'il vous plaît.
parts: et deux croissants, s'il vous plaît
lines.english: Two coffees and two croissants, please (if it pleases you).

lines.french: Non, je préfère une tartine beurrée pour le petit-déjeuner.
parts: Non, je préfère une tartine beurrée
lines.english: No, I prefer a slice of buttered bread for breakfast.

lines.french: Donc, deux‿expressos, un croissant et une tartine ?
parts: Donc, deux‿expressos, un croissant et une tartine
lines.english: So, two espressos, one croissant and one slice of buttered bread?

lines.french: Oui, c'est ça. Le croissant est pour moi et la tartine pour elle.
lines.english: Yes, that's right (this is it). The croissant is for me and the bread for her.

tests.title: Exercice 1 - Traduisez
tests.instructions: Listen, then rebuild the French sentence in order.

items.english: I prefer a croissant for breakfast.
The slice of bread is for her.
And the espresso is for me.
